newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and PIBOR futures finished higher on Friday in moderate volume in a market again turned optimistic which could quickly test its contract high of 126.80, dealers said.
Market-friendly U.S. data and statements judged conciliatory by Alexander Lebed after he was fired by Russion President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday, helped encourage investors, they said.
A sense that the public sector strike was not as widely followed as last year's labour action also lifted the market.
The franc firmed, too, trading firmly in a range between 3.3765 and 3.3807 per mark.
Dealers also said the the waves of selling which went through the market at the end of last week and on Wednesday helped flush out positions and left the market in a positive technical setting.
December PIBOR was also approaching its all-time high of 96.45, but traders said the contract's ability to rise much more was linked to the Bank of France's action on rates.
"At this three-month rate, which is glued to call money, you'll need a rate cut to see PIBOR at 96.50," one trader said.
The notionnel was also boosted when the U.S. 30 year bond futures contract went definitively through its 111 resistance.
At 1510 GMT, the Bond future was trading at 111.11, up seven ticks on the day.
There is little front rank economic news due from the United States next week, and dealers said that would create a good environment in which the notionnel contract could test 126.80.
